$comment: The hostile set of the dev library (`make dev-db`), declared once.
A library like this one is modelled by more than one fixture: `gen-devdb`
builds a real SQLite database the real engine reads, and a frontend's tests
may carry an in-memory fake of the same library that cannot reach that
database. Two fixtures modelling one library drift apart — a case one has
and the other lacks — unless something holds both to a single declaration.
So this file is the declaration and no fixture is. `devdb.rs`'s
`the_edge_cases_are_the_declared_ones` asserts the database against it, and
any other fixture of this library should be asserted against it the same
way. Adding a case to one fixture and not the other then fails on the side
that was not updated.
Hand-edited. Nothing generates it: a declaration generated from one of the
things it governs would agree with that one no matter how wrong it was,
which is `crates/corpus`' own rule about oracles.
`id` is positional — the hostile set is numbered 1..=n in this order, ahead
of the ordinary books, so a reviewer meets the cases and not the filler.
Behind them the database has two hundred ordinary books and, last, eighteen
books with two years of dated reads.
Fields are the intersection every fixture can honestly answer. Highlights,
notes and tags are deliberately absent: they live in side tables in the
database and need not exist in a fake at all, and a claim only one side can
check is decoration.

cases.title: A Book Of Zero Pages
cases.what: A false denominator: a percentage over this is a divide by zero, and the honest answer is that there is no percentage.

cases.title: A Book Of Unknown Length
cases.what: Absence, not zero. A progress bar has nothing to draw and must not draw an empty one.

cases.title: The Doorstop
cases.what: The fat end of the spine-thickness scale, and the ordinary progress case.

cases.title: A Pamphlet
cases.what: The thin end of the same scale, where a spine has no room for a title.

cases.title: A Book With No Cover At All
cases.what: cover_path is NULL. Not a broken image and not an apology — the empty state has to be a designed one. The only declared case with no cover, which is what makes the cover-bearing rules assertable.

cases.title: A Title Of Such Considerable And Frankly Self-Indulgent Length That It Cannot Possibly Fit In A Shelf Tile Or A Column Header, Being In The Manner Of The Long Eighteenth Century, Wherein The Title Was Also The Blurb
cases.what: A 220-character title. Clipping, wrapping, and the tooltip that should carry the rest.

cases.title: A Book Filed Under Surname
cases.what: Author stored as `Surname, Given` — the calibre and Goodreads form. Whether it is displayed that way is the engine's to derive, not a frontend template's.

cases.title: A Book By One Name
cases.what: A mononym author. Any name-splitting rule breaks here.

cases.title: A Book By Nobody
cases.what: No author at all — a real state after a bare epub import, not an error to report.

cases.title: A Book By Three People
cases.what: Three authors. Where the join and the truncation happen.

cases.title: A Book I Put Down
cases.what: An abandoned reading. Never styled as a failure. Shaped identically to an open read, which is why the state had to cross the wire.

cases.title: A Book I Went Back To
cases.what: Two readings, one finished and one open. A reading card is per reading, so this book has two of them — and `reading_state` reports the open one.

cases.title: A Book I Finished
cases.what: A finished reading. Carries no page: every frontend that had this case dropped the numbers for a word.

cases.title: 北回帰線のあたりで
cases.what: CJK title and author. Font fallback, and character-count-based clipping being wrong.

cases.title: الكتاب الذي يقرأ من اليمين
cases.what: An RTL title. Bidi layout, and a left-aligned column that should not be.

cases.title: Ærøskøbing: Ångström's Œuvre — a Naïve Façade
cases.what: Diacritics and ligatures, including ones that break a naive sort.

An empty title — the schema's own default, reachable from a sidecar with no doc_props. It is the empty string and NOT null: `books.title` is `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, so a stored book's title is never null however Option-shaped the DTO is. A fixture that models null here models a state the database cannot produce.

cases.title: The Claw Of The Conciliator
cases.what: A series with an index. `series_index` is a REAL and prints as `#2`, never `#2.0`; the label is derived by the engine.

cases.title: A Book In A Series With No Number
cases.what: A series naming no index. The pair moves together or not at all, and nothing is invented to fill the gap.

cases.title: A Book With Subjects And Shelves
cases.what: Provider subjects beside minted shelves — two different things that look alike, and one of the separations migration 0013 rests on.

cases.title: A Book Some Other App Touched
cases.what: A reading whose status is a word this build does not know. `readings.status` has no CHECK constraint, so this is reachable rather than invented; the engine answers it with `ReadingState::Other { raw }` rather than failing to parse. It is declared here so the database carries it too.
